body:
**Severity:** high. Fix in 0.2.8 (high/medium).

**Who is affected and why it matters:** Anyone who hand-edits AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and deletes the END marker of the devkb block: the next `devkb init` deletes their own text, and `--remove` deletes it again. Silent data loss in a file devkb does not own.

**Reproduce:**
```
AGENTS.md = "# Team\n" + BEGIN + "\nold block (END deleted)\n\n## IMPORTANT USER SECTION\nkeep me\n"
devkb init; devkb init      # user section gone
devkb init --remove          # file is now "# Team\n"
```

**Actual:** the non-greedy block regex matches from the orphan BEGIN to the END of the newly appended block, removing everything between.

**Expected:** an unpaired BEGIN or END marker makes init refuse to touch that file, with a message naming the file and line; no user text is ever removed.

**Done when:** a test with an orphan BEGIN and user text after it fails on `main` and passes: the file is byte-identical after init and after --remove, and init reports the refusal.

Found by the 0.2.5 → 0.2.8 quality audit (main at `4369145`); reproduced twice, by the reviewer and independently.
title: devkb init keeps a user's AGENTS.md text when a devkb block has lost its end marker
